image-alt-not-descriptive: Confirm the candidate concerns an exposed image with a present text alternative. Missing alt/text alternative is a syntax issue, not this semantic type. Compare the saved alternative text or accessible image name with image content, purpose, surrounding context, and visual evidence when available. Choose uncertain when image content or purpose is not grounded.
video-captions-inaccurate: Confirm this is a visible video with a captions track and saved ordered cue text. Compare the semantic caption content with supplied spoken narration or authoritative transcript evidence when available. Judge semantic content accuracy, not caption presence, WebVTT syntax, or timing accuracy unless timing evidence is explicitly part of the candidate. Choose uncertain when narration or authoritative reference evidence is absent, incomplete, or ambiguous.
lang-mismatch: Confirm this is page-level language, with a valid root/page language declaration and visible page text. Do not use this type for missing lang, invalid language codes, or local passage language. Compare the declared page language with dominant saved page content and choose uncertain if the dominant language or declaration is not grounded.
language-of-parts-mismatch: Confirm a passage or component has a present local language declaration. Missing local lang is not this type. Compare the declared local language with the actual language of the saved passage text, using surrounding page language only as context. Choose uncertain for short, ambiguous, proper-name, code, or insufficient text evidence.
link-text-mismatch: Confirm this is an exposed link with present text or accessible name. Compare the label/name with destination, href meaning, same-page target, matched destination state, or next-state evidence when available. Do not fetch external targets or treat absent destination evidence as proof. Choose uncertain when destination or purpose cannot be grounded.
button-label-mismatch: Confirm this is an exposed button with a present label or accessible name. Compare the label/name with the saved button purpose, local context, trigger/action evidence, and resulting state when available. Generic labels may be resolved by direct context; conflicting labels or results support violation. Choose uncertain when action/result evidence is missing or ambiguous.
form-label-mismatch: Confirm this is an exposed form control with an associated label or accessible name. Missing labels are syntax concerns. Compare the label/name with the field purpose using control attributes, directly associated labels/descriptions, form/group context, and observable state. Do not rely on hidden benchmark intent; choose uncertain when actual field purpose is not grounded.
widget-label-purpose-mismatch: Confirm this is a labeled interactive widget such as a tab, menu item, accordion/disclosure, tree item, option, or custom control. Compare the label/name with role/type, controlled or revealed content, surrounding context, and resulting/next state when available. Do not judge solely from role syntax; choose uncertain if controlled content or result is unavailable.
heading-not-descriptive: Confirm this is a present heading. Compare the heading text or accessible name with the content, section, state, or purpose it introduces, using heading scope and transition context when relevant. Short, repeated, or broad headings are not violations by themselves. Choose uncertain when the introduced content or state purpose is incomplete or contradictory.
landmark-purpose-mismatch: Confirm this is a structurally valid landmark or named region. Compare the landmark role and accessible label with its own scoped content and surrounding document structure. Structural landmark count/nesting failures are not this type. Choose uncertain when landmark boundaries, label source, or contained content are not grounded.
page-title-not-descriptive: Confirm the page title is present. Compare it with the saved page or SPA state purpose using title, route, top headings, body excerpt, dialog/state context, and graph context when available. Do not require exact title/H1 equality. Choose uncertain if current state purpose cannot be established.
autocomplete-purpose-mismatch: Confirm an exposed input has a present syntactically valid autocomplete value. Missing or invalid autocomplete syntax is not this semantic type unless a semantic purpose conflict is also grounded. Compare the token purpose with the field purpose from label/name, placeholder, form/group context, and directly connected instructions. Choose uncertain when either purpose is unclear.
aria-state-mismatch: Confirm a valid ARIA state or property such as aria-expanded, aria-selected, aria-checked, or aria-pressed is present. Compare the declared value with current rendered or interaction state, controlled targets, peer state, and screenshot/context when available. Do not treat unsupported/invalid ARIA syntax as this type. Choose uncertain when rendered state is not observable.
table-header-association-mismatch: Confirm table header associations are structurally present and resolved to real headers. Broken or missing references are syntax issues. Compare data-cell content with associated header text, row/column position, table caption, and surrounding table meaning. Choose uncertain when the table relationship meaning is insufficiently captured.
error-message-mismatch: Confirm an associated error message is present for an invalid or validation state. Missing error messages are not this semantic type. Compare the message text with the control label, field purpose, current value state, native/ARIA validity, and directly saved validation context. Choose uncertain when the actual invalid input or validation reason is not grounded.
